She moved with the fluidity of water, yet her strikes were as hard as stone. Her eyes were a piercing amber that seemed to read the soul of anyone who dared to cross her path. The only thing that made her seem more terrifying than her training was the way she carried herself—confident, unyielding, and utterly unbothered by the chaos she left in her wake.

Manson, who had built his empire on fear, had a simple rule: if a minion displeased him, he would have Priscilla punish them.
